html:
The Dharawal are the Aboriginal Australian peoples who shared the Dharawal language, along the coast south of Sydney through what is now Wollongong, Port Kembla and Nowra in New South Wales. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

They lived in clans of hunters, fishers and gatherers, using bark canoes on the bays and the sea. In April 1770 James Cook landed at Kurnell on the south shore of Botany Bay, in the country of the Gweagal, a Dharawal clan. Two men opposed the landing; Cook's party fired on them and took their spears and shields. Eighteen years later the First Fleet arrived in the same bay.

In 1816 soldiers sent by Governor Lachlan Macquarie killed Dharawal and Gundungurra people in the Appin massacre. Neighbours included the Dharug to the north, the Gundungurra to the west and the Yuin to the south. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
